course_name_en: Control and Safety of Refrigeration Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Students can develop and validate control engineering models for refrigeration and air conditioning systems by applying methods of parameter identification and simulation, selecting and parameterizing controllers, and implementing digital control algorithms to realize energy-efficient and stable system controls in practice.

Students can analyze legal requirements and safety-related aspects in the manufacturing and operation of refrigeration systems by performing risk analyses, including designing pressure relief devices, planning functional safety devices, and applying ATEX regulations to ensure safe operation and standard-compliant design of refrigeration systems.

syllabus_topics: Selected methods of control engineering for refrigeration and air conditioning technology
Design methods for controllers (root locus, frequency response)
Structure and function of various expansion valves and simulation models for expansion valves.
Design of pressure relief devices (real fluids and two-phase flow)
Functional safety (lifecycle model, reliability and documentation requirements)
Consequence analysis and effects of disturbances and substance releases
Fundamentals of explosion protection and ATEX directive
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of equally weighted graded written or oral examinations for each partial performance. A laboratory work is a prerequisite for MABM142B. The examination format is determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
bibliography: Will be provided per semester (additions based on current technical developments)
